binders: A type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
An implicit measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
A nonnegative real exponent p together with a proof that 1≤p.
Real-valued functions X:Ω→Real in the two conclusions.
hypotheses: p is a finite nonnegative real satisfying 1≤p.
For the second conclusion only, X is almost-everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ.
conclusions: For every function X:Ω→Real, the Luxemburg-type gauge associated with the constructed power function x↦x^p equals eLpNorm X p μ as an ENNReal value.
For every a.e.-strongly-measurable X:Ω→Real, finiteness of that Luxemburg-type gauge is equivalent to MeasureTheory.MemLp X p μ.
mathematical_definitions: The constructed function ψp is x↦x^(p.toReal); for p≥1 it is nonnegative, convex and nondecreasing on [0,∞), maps 0 to 0, and tends to ∞ at ∞.
For ψ, μ, and X, the gauge is inf {t∈ENNReal:t≠0, t≠∞, and ∫⁻ψ(|X(ω)|/t.toReal)dμ≤1}.
Finite-gauge membership means that this ENNReal gauge is strictly below ∞.
MeasureTheory.MemLp X p μ means X is a.e.-strongly measurable and eLpNorm X p μ is finite.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space and for every finite exponent p≥1, construct ψp(x)=x^p. Then for every real-valued function X, its Luxemburg gauge defined using ψp and threshold 1 is exactly its extended Lp norm. Moreover, for every a.e.-strongly-measurable X, having finite Luxemburg gauge is equivalent to belonging to Lp.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure is restricted to a probability measure, although the displayed gauge and Lp norm are meaningful for more general measures.
The exponent is a finite NNReal satisfying p≥1; the cases p=∞ and 0≤p<1 are excluded.
The first equality quantifies over all real-valued functions, without a measurability hypothesis.
The membership equivalence is conditional on a.e.-strong measurability; MemLp itself also includes that condition.
The scale infimum is taken in ENNReal, but admissible scales exclude both 0 and ∞, so they correspond to positive finite real scales.
The proposition concerns raw functions Ω→Real and extended norm values, not equivalence classes modulo almost-everywhere equality.
The constructed power function is defined on all reals by Real.rpow, but its structural axioms and every gauge evaluation relevant here use nonnegative inputs.
